summary: Attempt 2 of Owner amendment A0017 (layer CONTRACT; targets T087, T088, T102), repairing exactly the two findings independent review-001 required and changing nothing else. (1) POSITIVE HETEROGENEOUS-SCHEMA VERIFICATION: T102's acceptance now carries the positive case the recorded direction and A0014:T102:consume-schema-bound-robustness require under VERIFICATION - the walk-forward evaluation is exercised positively over at least two heterogeneous registered T068 strategy identities whose declared parameter schemas differ in axis names, types, units or ranges, each built from its own evaluated run's validated T105 manifest and its own registered schema revision, each surface recording the registry and schema identity, version and checksum it was built from, deterministic per schema under repeated construction, and a point one of the two schemas declares is still refused for the schema that does not declare it (test, fixture) - so the attempt-1 impact assessment's positive-heterogeneity claim is now supported by the contract text at todo/phases/P10-research-and-models/T102.md:83-92 instead of standing unverified. (2) OCCURRENCE ARITHMETIC: this record re-measures and states the counts and names the superseded wording - T087.md carries five `T063` tokens (at :36, :58, :63, :65, :73), superseding the attempt-1 phrase 'the three remaining `T063` tokens in the edited file (T087.md:36, :58, :63, :65, :73)'; T088's four (:44, :67, :71, :79) are confirmed; T102's seven `T064` tokens are confirmed and re-measured for this candidate at :60, :62, :94, :97, :101, :117, :119 (moved from :60, :62, :87, :90, :94, :110, :112 by the seven lines the inserted clause adds above them), and every remaining occurrence in all three files is a legacy-only rendering or prohibition with no normative consumption. Everything else is unchanged from the reviewed candidate 1078d055d24f700e1b97a89bb7211108d25bca2f: T087 and T088 replace the normative T063 authority with T105 read through their existing T069 dependency (no duplicate edge; T069's configured dependency list carries T105) while keeping legacy T063 manifests read-only, labelled historical and never parsed as current, failing closed on failed, cancelled, missing or revision-mismatched runs and carrying positive, negative, migration-fixture and old-path-unreachable verification; T102 gains T106 as a direct dependency and consumes it as the current schema-bound robustness protocol, its model-backed component obtains a registered T068 identity that a T069 run request must name, and the A0013 identity finding on T102 is repaired in the same contract. Exactly four open impacts are closed - A0014:T087:read-current-manifest-coverage, A0014:T088:reconcile-current-result-checksums, A0013:T102:legacy and A0014:T102:consume-schema-bound-robustness; the other fourteen stay open and are named.
rationale: Owner direction executed inside the CONTRACT layer, inside the three named targets only, with the two findings of independent review-001 repaired and nothing else changed; every pre-existing obligation, acceptance clause and Must-not clause of the three contracts is preserved. ATTEMPT-2 REPAIR 1 - POSITIVE HETEROGENEOUS-SCHEMA VERIFICATION (review-001 required change 1). The recorded direction requires T102's verification to cover 'positive evaluation over heterogeneous registered schemas' (todo/amendments/A0017/request.json), and A0014:T102:consume-schema-bound-robustness records the same under VERIFICATION ('positive evaluation for heterogeneous registered schemas'). The reviewed candidate carried every other item of that disposition but no positive-heterogeneity clause, while its impact assessment claimed one. This attempt takes the finding's first option and adds the clause to the target contract instead of weakening the claim: todo/phases/P10-research-and-models/T102.md:83-92 now requires that 'the same evaluation runs positively over at least two heterogeneous registered T068 strategy identities whose declared parameter schemas differ in axis names, types, units or ranges, each built from its own evaluated run's validated T105 manifest and its own registered schema revision, each surface recording the registry and schema identity, version and checksum it was built from, deterministic per schema under repeated construction, and a point one of the two schemas declares is still refused for the schema that does not declare it (test, fixture)'. The clause makes the heterogeneity test real rather than transitive: two registered identities whose schemas genuinely differ, each surface built only from its own identity's schema revision, and a cross-schema refusal - a point valid for one schema is still refused for the other - covered by test and fixture. The change is purely additive and measured as such: difflib between the reviewed candidate 1078d055d24f700e1b97a89bb7211108d25bca2f and this candidate produces exactly one replace hunk (base lines 83-85, candidate lines 83-92), and the white-space-normalised candidate text with the inserted clause removed is byte-equal to the base text, so no clause was removed, reordered or weakened. The claim in this attempt's impact_assessment.verification is that contract text, not an assertion about T106's own acceptance. ATTEMPT-2 REPAIR 2 - OCCURRENCE ARITHMETIC (review-001 required change 2). The attempt-1 record's sentence 'the three remaining `T063` tokens in the edited file (T087.md:36, :58, :63, :65, :73)' is superseded by this record's re-measured count: todo/phases/P08-operations-and-web/T087.md carries five `T063` tokens, on exactly the five lines it listed (:36, :58, :63, :65, :73; grep -o counts five). T088.md's four `T063` tokens (:44, :67, :71, :79) are confirmed. T102.md's seven `T064` tokens are confirmed and re-measured for this candidate at :60, :62, :94, :97, :101, :117, :119 - the attempt-1 positions :60, :62, :87, :90, :94, :110, :112 moved by the seven lines the inserted clause adds above them. planner-001.json cannot be corrected in place: for a CONTRACT amendment the controller permits changes only inside the target contracts and todo/config.yaml (tools/workflow/core.py:1707-1716 for the allowed paths, with the config-field drift rule at :1717-1735), so the correction is recorded here, as A0016 attempt 2 recorded its citation repair for a record it also could not edit. The substantive claim is unchanged and review-001 verified it true: every remaining occurrence in the three files is a legacy-only rendering, an explicit prohibition or a negative test case, never a live authority. T087 (todo/phases/P08-operations-and-web/T087.md): the normative T063 reference is replaced by T105 as the range and coverage authority - the References entry reads 'T105 (the registry-bound manifest and coverage a range selection and a run result are read against, reached through this task's T069 dependency rather than as a duplicate edge)' - and the Deliverables require the range selection to resolve its coverage from the validated T105 registry-bound manifest of a T069 run and to display, as recorded, the dataset version, the member pool and its block range, the covering run identity, and the registry revision and parameter-schema identity and version the coverage was produced under, with the run list resolving every coverage and provenance field it shows through the validated T105 manifest linked by that run rather than restating it from the page. A further paragraph keeps a legacy pre-registry `T063` manifest read-only and byte-identical and historical-only, with no coverage interval, registry revision, parameter-schema identity or strategy identity ever inferred, substituted or backfilled from it, and makes a failed, cancelled, missing or revision-mismatched run show the `WEB-GLOBAL-002` fail-closed evidence state with no selectable coverage and no result, while a requested range outside the coverage the current manifest records is refused rather than silently widened. Acceptance carries the positive T105-backed range display with the recorded provenance and identical repeated renders, the negative refusals for a legacy `T063` manifest, a manifest that is not the validated current artifact of its run, an unregistered strategy identity and a registry, schema or code revision that disagrees with the recorded revision, the failed-or-cancelled no-selectable-coverage case, a migration fixture keeping every legacy `T063` manifest and its checksums byte-identical and visibly legacy, and an old-path-unreachable assertion proving no current page or API path can consult the predecessor `T063` hard-coded-identity manifest as a current authority. Must not adds the matching prohibitions, and dependencies stay T068, T069, T084 exactly as recorded because the direction asks to keep T069 as the product-run dependency and to confirm its amended closure carries T105 rather than adding a duplicate edge: todo/config.yaml:735-744 lists T105 in T069's depends_on (measured), and an independent DFS over the configured graph finds no cycle and puts T105 in T087's closure (44 tasks). Closes A0014:T087:read-current-manifest-coverage. T088 (todo/phases/P08-operations-and-web/T088.md): T063 is replaced by T105 as the checksum and provenance authority the same way, on the measured basis that todo/config.yaml:928-934 gives T088 the dependencies T069, T084 and T069 carries T105. The Deliverables render 'the validated T105 manifest and coverage its T069 run published'; a paragraph requires the result, coverage and attribution checksums to reconcile solely against the validated T105 manifest linked by the chosen T069 run, and renders the `WEB-GLOBAL-002` fail-closed state - with the reason shown instead of a number or a complete-looking chart - for a checksum that does not reconcile, a manifest that is not the validated current artifact of its run, a registry, schema or code revision that disagrees with the recorded revision, and a failed, cancelled or incomplete run; a historical result or manifest stays byte-identical under an explicit legacy, non-current marker whose registry, schema or checksum fields are never inferred, and it grants the read surface no approval, execution or promotion authority. Acceptance carries the positive checksum trace that reconciles each displayed checksum to the validated T105 manifest, the negative tamper, mismatch, wrong-revision and non-current-artifact blocking cases, a migration fixture keeping the historical results and their `T063` manifests byte-identical and visibly legacy together with a compatibility fixture rendering them explicitly non-current and never reconciled against as current authority, the failed, cancelled or incomplete no-complete-looking-result case, and old-path-unreachable coverage proving no current display path reconciles against the predecessor `T063` hard-coded-identity manifest. Must not adds the matching prohibitions. Every result-display obligation of the contract is preserved, measured clause by clause: the price series with the Range band and the entry, increase, decrease, collect, rebalance and exit markers, the equity chart with drawdown, the PnL attribution with its explicit unexplained residual, the inventory chart with `liquidity` and both tokens' raw integer amounts, the tick liquidity distribution, the coverage chart that draws a gap as a gap, the price-never-replaced and `liquidityDelta`-never-a-currency rules, the `WEB-GLOBAL-007` layering, the `RELATIVE_ONLY` case and the absent-manifest unknown state are all unchanged. Closes A0014:T088:reconcile-current-result-checksums. T102 (todo/phases/P10-research-and-models/T102.md): T106 is added as a direct dependency - the Dependencies line reads 'T061, T101, T106' and todo/config.yaml:1095-1099 carries the identical sorted, duplicate-free list - and T064 is replaced by T106 as the current robustness and anti-overfitting protocol everywhere it was normative, with T064 surviving only as the successor's declared replacement dependency and as explicitly legacy read-only artifacts, which is what T106.md:45-48 requires of a later CONTRACT amendment. The walk-forward Deliverable consumes T106 as the current schema-bound protocol: every parameter-surface axis is built from the exact registered identity and parameter-schema revision the evaluated run's validated T105 manifest records, every axis name, type, unit and value is declared by that schema and inside its declared range, and the registry and schema identity, version and checksum are recorded with the surface and with the report. A fail-closed Deliverable makes missing, legacy-only or revision-mismatched T106 evidence yield `UNCERTAIN` or `NO_TRADE` for the affected configuration or block publication of the robustness conclusion, and refuses to evaluate a model-backed strategy whose registered identity, parameter schema or code binding is missing, unregistered or mismatched, with neither case falling back to the unrestricted `T064` predecessor surface, to an inferred or default identity or to an unqualified baseline; a further Deliverable keeps legacy `T064` robustness artifacts read-only, byte-identical and never current. The A0013 finding on this task is repaired in the same contract and not by a second mechanism: the Outcome places the model-backed implementation under a registered T068 strategy identity - registered through the T068 registry rather than through a second registry of its own - with a parameter schema, a version and code provenance, reached only when a run names that registered identity through the T069 run entry point, refusing an identity the registry does not carry rather than inferring, defaulting or substituting it; the first Deliverable bullet requires that identity and forbids requesting the component by its implementation module, by a free-text name or by an unregistered or inferred identity, and states that the schema declares the tunable parameters with their names, types, units and ranges. The pre-existing deterministic fallback to the rule-based baseline is preserved and scoped so it cannot be used as a bypass: it covers the model artifact's availability only and never substitutes for the registered identity, for a validated manifest or for the current schema-bound robustness evidence. Acceptance carries the positive T105-manifest plus T106-surface resolution with the recorded registry/schema identity, version and checksum and deterministic repeated construction, the positive heterogeneous-schema clause this attempt adds (T102.md:83-92, described above), the negative undeclared, out-of-range, wrong-unit, wrong-type and wrong-revision cases rejected before any fold is evaluated, the missing, legacy-only or mismatched T106 fail-closed case, the refusal of an unregistered identity and of a run request that does not name a registered identity, a migration fixture keeping a legacy `T064` artifact byte-identical and labelled legacy with incompatible revisions never merged into one sensitivity conclusion, and an old-path-unreachable test proving current evaluation cannot construct a parameter surface through the unrestricted `T064` builder; the boundary list gains a registered strategy whose T106 surface is missing or from an incompatible revision, and a legacy robustness artifact offered as current evaluation evidence. Must not names T070 as the central risk gateway that model and robustness evidence may neither weaken nor bypass and forbids model or robustness evidence granting execution, approval or promotion authority, forbids falling back to the unrestricted `T064` surface or to an unqualified baseline when the current schema-bound evidence is missing, legacy or mismatched, and forbids treating a legacy `T064` artifact or an unregistered, inferred or default identity as current evidence; every original clause is preserved. References name T106 as the current protocol, G-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-01 and G-ML-01 as the governing goals, and T068, T069, T105 - each marked as reached through T101 (measured: T102's closure of 44 tasks contains T068, T069, T101, T105 and T106) - with T070 named without a dependency edge because the prohibition it anchors is a boundary the task may not cross, not work it consumes. Closes A0014:T102:consume-schema-bound-robustness and A0013:T102:legacy. DEPENDENCY FACTS, re-measured at this candidate: each edited contract's Dependencies line equals its configured list, sorted and duplicate-free (T087 'T068, T069, T084'; T088 'T069, T084'; T102 'T061, T101, T106'); an independent DFS over the configured graph finds no cycle; each target's closure is 44 tasks, T087's and T088's contain T105 and T102's contains T105 and T106, which is what T105.md:54-59 and T106.md:45-48 ask of a later CONTRACT amendment. After this change no ordinary PLANNED consumer remains on T063 (consumers T064 APPROVED and T105 its successor) or on T064 (consumers T065 and T066 APPROVED and T106 its successor), which is the precondition for retiring either predecessor; this amendment retires nothing, sets no superseded_by and changes no status. RESOLVED IMPACTS: recomputed with the workflow's own rules, exactly four of the eighteen impacts open at the attempt base are closed here, each on a targeted task and each matching its recorded required_disposition - A0014:T087:read-current-manifest-coverage (contract, dependency, implementation, data, operations, security and verification dispositions all represented in the edited contract, including the positive T105-backed range display, the negative cases, the migration fixture and the old-path-unreachable assertion), A0014:T088:reconcile-current-result-checksums (same, with the positive checksum trace), A0013:T102:legacy (the registered identity and the naming of that identity by a run request) and A0014:T102:consume-schema-bound-robustness (T106 as the current protocol with a direct dependency, fail-closed missing/legacy/mismatched handling, T070 untouched as the risk boundary, and the verification the disposition requires, now including the positive heterogeneous-schema evaluation this attempt adds). The remaining fourteen stay open, untouched and named: A0013:T063:legacy, A0013:T064:legacy, A0013:T066:legacy and A0013:T067:legacy (the four retirement-route findings, which only SUPERSEDE can close and which this amendment deliberately does not attempt), A0013:T071:legacy, A0013:T072:legacy, A0013:T082:legacy, A0013:T085:legacy, A0013:T086:legacy, A0013:T091:legacy, A0013:T096:legacy, A0013:T103:legacy, A0013:T104:legacy and A0014:T096:include-successor-final-evidence. AFFECTED EXISTING TASKS: empty because this change edits no governing document - the Owner direction for A0017 leaves docs/intent/ and docs/spec/ untouched and this record changed no other task contract - so no existing contract is left asserting something a governing document no longer says; the pre-existing T086 and T103 findings and the research-page run trigger remain the already-recorded A0013 impacts named above, not new conflicts. impact_assessment.implementation: No implementation change is possible or required in this layer: T087, T088 and T102 are PLANNED at attempt 0, and src/robinhood_lp has no `web` and no `models` module (measured), so the two pages and the model harness do not exist yet. The contracts direct the future implementation: no current page, API or evaluation path may parse the predecessor hard-coded-identity manifest or the unrestricted `T064` parameter-surface builder as current, each of the three contracts carries an old-path-unreachable acceptance test, and T102's evaluation must now be exercised positively over at least two heterogeneous registered schemas as well. The predecessor code that will be adapted or replaced - src/robinhood_lp/reports/ (the manifest authority, whose hard-coded VALID_STRATEGY_KINDS vocabulary at src/robinhood_lp/reports/manifest.py:118 T105 replaces) and src/robinhood_lp/robustness/surfaces.py (T064's generic parameter surface, which T106 constrains) - stays exactly where T105's and T106's own Replacement and migration sections place it and was not edited.
impact_assessment.data: Historical artifacts stay byte-identical and read-only, and the three contracts say so: legacy pre-registry `T063` manifests and historical results are labelled historical and non-current, their checksums are preserved, and none of their registry, schema, checksum, coverage or identity fields may be inferred, substituted or backfilled; legacy `T064` robustness artifacts stay read-only and explicitly legacy and are consumed only in an explicitly labelled compatibility analysis; incompatible registry or schema revisions are never merged into one sensitivity conclusion. The migration fixtures the direction requires are named as acceptance evidence in all three contracts. This attempt added no data obligation and touched no stored artifact, manifest, checksum or dataset.
impact_assessment.operations: The operational boundary is explicit in each contract and unchanged by this attempt: T087 offers no selectable coverage and no result for a failed, cancelled, missing or revision-mismatched run and refuses a range outside the recorded coverage instead of widening it; T088 renders no complete-looking result, chart or reconciled figure for a failed, cancelled or incomplete run; and T102 yields `UNCERTAIN` or `NO_TRADE` or blocks publication of the robustness conclusion when current T106 evidence is missing, legacy-only or mismatched. The cutover avoids two authoritative paths by construction: T105 and T106 remain the single current manifest and robustness authorities, T069 remains the single owner of the product-run lifecycle, T068 remains the single registry, and the three edited contracts only read through them, so nothing in this amendment creates a second publisher, runner, registry or surface builder. The new positive clause adds an evaluation matrix over two registered schemas, not a second evaluation path.
impact_assessment.security: No credential, endpoint secret or key material is involved: the additions are read-surface provenance, fail-closed display, validation boundaries and a positive evaluation matrix, and the governing contracts (T105, T106, T068) are already non-secret and deterministic. The registry display and page availability still grant no approval, execution or promotion authority and reveal no secrets (T087's and T088's original Must-not clauses are preserved and extended), and T102 names T070 as the central risk gateway that model and robustness evidence may neither weaken nor bypass, with G-ML-01 as the governing statement that models produce no paper or live authority. This attempt adds no permission, no path and no execution surface, and no security-relevant file was edited.
